steps.prompt: Before the check: which part of this unit feels easiest, and which do you want to look at again?

cards.title: Adjectives: quick review
cards.body: Adjectives describe nouns: what kind (muddy), which one (that, last), how many (three, several). They go before a noun or after a linking verb (the room was silent). Pick precise ones, not nice, good or great.

cards.title: Comparisons: quick review
cards.body: Two things: -er or more (faster than, more careful than). Three or more: -est or most (the fastest, the most careful). Short words take -er/-est; long words take more/most; never both. Irregular: good, better, best; bad, worse, worst.

cards.title: Adverbs: quick review
cards.body: Adverbs tell how (carefully, well), when (yesterday, finally) and where (outside, upstairs). After an action verb, use the adverb: played well, ran quickly. After a linking verb, use the adjective: feels good, went quiet. Swap “very + weak word” for one strong word.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll write a short paragraph that shows off everything you’ve learned. Quill gives it a score.

prompts: What did you learn about adjectives or adverbs that you didn’t know before this unit?
Which describing-word habit will you check for when you write your next essay?
